newsitem.title: USA: Maine Gov signs $3.8 bln state budget.
newsitem.headline: Maine Gov signs $3.8 bln state budget.

text.p: Maine Gov. Angus King signed Wednesday a $3.8 billion state operational budget that was enacted more than three months before the end of the state's fiscal year.
King said the two-year spending package will slow the growth of state government, provide $220 million in tax relief and increase aid to local communities by $104 million.
"(This) is a great budget for Maine kids, Maine people and Maine taxpayers," King told reporters at a state house signing ceremony that included Democratic legislative leaders.
King, an independent, dismissed Republican complaints that the budget quickly pushed through the legislative process by Democrats was not bipartisan.
"In the end, the difference between the parties was less than one percent of the total biennial budget," King told reporters.

Legislators gave final approval to the spending package late Tuesday rejecting Republican efforts to push for additional tax cuts and an income tax cap tha was scheduled to take effect at the end of the fiscal year June 30.
By approving the budget April 1, Democrats took advantage of a parlimentary rule that allowed the budget to be passed by a simple majority rather than a two-thirds marjority.
Democrats do not have a two-thirds majority in either the House or Senate, and some Republicans had threatened to use their voting block to shut state government.
Republican leaders vowed the fight was not over, and predicted that bills still being considered would force the budget's bottom line to be increased.
Republicans also accused Democrats of including several items - including $500,000 to create a family court system - without public hearings or proper debate.

The decision to approve the budget before April 1 means legislators will have to adjourn this session later this week, but King said he will call them back into special session to consider unfinished business.
Issues before lawmakers include King's proposal to double the cigarette tax, electric deregulation, and whether enact a ban on same-sex marriages or put the measure to voters in November.
King said the early approval of the budget should set an example for future legislatures, because it will allow them to debate policy issues without "the rumble of the budget in he background."
